topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors as Spatial Guides

sections.title: What is a Vector? (Visualizing Movement)
lecture_lines: Vectors are directed segments in 2D space.
They represent magnitude and specific direction.
Think of them as instructions for movement.
animations: Create a 2D arrow representing a vector from origin #FFD700 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg]
Show vector movement animation with trail #FFFFFF
Highlight vector components X and Y #FF4500 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg]

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule
lecture_lines: Place the second tail at the first head.
The resultant vector connects origin to finish.
animations: Draw resultant vector from start to finish #FFD700
Move vector two to show equivalence [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg] #FF4500

sections.title: Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks
lecture_lines: Basis vectors i and j are building blocks.
Any 2D vector is their linear combination.
animations: Draw unit vector i_hat at (1,0) #00FFFF with background [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg]
Show linear combination as weighted sum #FF4500

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Vectors combine instructions for spatial transformation.
They form the basis for coordinate systems.
Linear algebra enables complex visual movement.
